step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Analyze Visual Inventory & Audio Transcript:
   - Physical sensors on production machines send pulses to AWS Greengrass edge gateways (one per machine).
   - AWS Greengrass local counting engine aggregates sensor events and sends count messages via AWS IoT Core rules to trigger a Lambda function ('Lambda Ingestion').
   - Lambda Ingestion calculates and updates the machine state in Amazon DynamoDB.
   - Shop floor operators use a smartphone/tablet application powered by AWS Amplify to view real-time state and submit container completion reports.
   - Amplify calls Amazon API Gateway, which forwards requests to a backend Lambda function ('Lambda API').
   - Lambda API reads real-time machine state from DynamoDB and pushes completed container event reports to Amazon SQS.
   - Amazon SQS queues batch messages and delivers them to an external ERP system.
2. Pruning & Node Rules:
   - Generic human actor icon 'User' is pruned according to Rule 5.
   - Non-AWS services ('Sensor' and 'ERP') are mapped to 'ThirdParty'.
   - Dual Lambda functions perform distinct architectural roles (Ingestion vs API), so they are preserved as distinct nodes.
3. Logical Edge & Flow Segmentation:
   - Flow 0 (Ingestion): Sensor -> Greengrass -> Lambda Ingestion -> DynamoDB.
   - Flow 1 (User App & Reporting): Amplify -> API Gateway -> Lambda API -> DynamoDB / SQS -> ERP.

graph.name: Maxinear Real-time Piece Counting Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture for real-time piece counting on manufacturing shop floor using AWS IoT Greengrass, Lambda, DynamoDB, Amplify, API Gateway, SQS, and ERP integration.

nodes.name: Sensor
nodes.notes: Physical sensor attached to production machines that detects bolts falling through light grids.

nodes.name: Greengrass
nodes.notes: Edge gateway running local counting engine to transform varying sensor messages.

nodes.name: Lambda Ingestion
nodes.notes: Triggered via AWS IoT Core rules to derive machine states from incoming count messages.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Stores current real-time machine state data.

nodes.name: Amplify
nodes.notes: Hosts and powers smartphone and tablet application for shop floor operators.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Provides API endpoints for the shop floor application.

nodes.name: Lambda API
nodes.notes: Queries DynamoDB state for the user application and processes reported batch/container completion events.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Queues reported container events before sending batch updates to the external ERP system.

nodes.name: ERP
nodes.notes: External ERP system receiving batch production reports.

edges.notes: Sensor sends pulses to AWS Greengrass edge gateway upon bolt detection.
AWS Greengrass sends local count messages via AWS IoT Core rules to trigger Lambda Ingestion.
Lambda Ingestion writes updated machine state into DynamoDB.
Amplify mobile app calls API Gateway endpoints to fetch state and submit reports.
API Gateway forwards application requests to Lambda API.
Lambda API reads state data from DynamoDB.
Lambda API sends completed container events to SQS.
SQS delivers queued report updates to external ERP system.
